title: Stash and Choreography — Weekly Ops & Standup Digest
content:
Week: 2029-11-05 to 2029-11-11
Owners: Priya Menon (editor), Evan Liu (ops), Sofia Ruiz (kernel), Marcus Hale (measurements)

Summary (TL;DR):
- Rolled the prefill choreographer prototype into a canary pool; observed 9% end-to-end tail latency improvement for conversational flows with long prefix reuse.
- Detected an unusual eviction cascade in the KV shadow cache during a synthetic spike; root cause appears to be interaction between the new LRU+score heuristic and an aggressively short item TTL under certain traffic patterns.
- Microbatch jitter under 8-token bursts shows bimodal latency distribution; hypothesis: scheduling quantization at GPU queue boundary.
- Action items assigned for hardening the kernel handshake path and introducing a conservative fallback mode for the choreographer when cache pressure crosses threshold.

Monday standup notes (quick check-ins):
- Priya: Canary rollout started; 20 instances, canary traffic routed by experiment flag. Watching cost and anomalies.
- Evan: Observability dashboards added: per-prefill hit ratio, eviction waterfall, and cache headroom. Instrumentation PR merged.
- Sofia: Kernel handshake patch (optimistic-kv-lock) landed on branch; initial microbench results positive on p99 for single-token steps.
- Marcus: Ran three synthetic traffic patterns (chatty, bursty, longprefix); uploaded CSVs to the shared bucket.

Deep dives / Notes from weekly sync (Wed 11/07):
1) Prefill Choreographer (design + runtime observations)
   - What we shipped: a choreography layer that sequences prefill requests to the KV cache and kernel prefetch pipeline with backpressure signals instead of blind fanout. Canary config: threshold=0.6 hit_rate, two-stage backoff (20ms then 60ms).
   - Observed impact: average CPU on canary nodes up 4% but tail latency (99th) for chat flows down 9%. Cost per token ~ unchanged due to reduced wasted kernel cold starts.
   - Problems seen: when the choreographer encountered a sudden surge of novel prefixes, it attempted to prefill aggressively; under existing eviction TTL settings this triggered cascade evictions which then caused fallback path thrashing.
   - Short-term mitigation: add a soft limit (prefill_budget) per logical cohort and a debounce window for identical prefix prefetches.

2) KV Shadow Cache Eviction Cascade Investigation
   - Repro steps: replayed the bursty synthetic trace JIRA-RT-2389 at 2x QPS for 120s against a small cluster with default TTL 30s.
   - Findings: The new LRUScore amortizes by frequency but with short TTLs frequency resets faster than expected. When many low-frequency items are added, score sorting temporarily ranks older large-value items lower, triggering multiple evictions and re-fetch waves.
   - Proposed fixes: increase min-TTL to 90s for items larger than 1KB, or prefer size-aware eviction (score - alpha*size).
   - Test plan: run A/B with size-aware eviction enabled on 10% of serving capacity for 48h.

3) Microbatch jitter analysis
   - Symptom: 8-token microbatches show p95 at 34ms and p99 at 78ms with a cluster p99 spike to 120ms under combined load.
   - Hypothesis: job coalescer rounding aligns batches into uneven GPU dispatch windows; the scheduler wakes and sends 1-2 extra wakeups due to clock alignment.
   - Experiment: added clock-slip randomization (+/- 3ms) to batching tick and measured smoothing; early results show p99 reduced by ~15% in lab. Next step is to run with traffic mix.

4) Kernel handshake hardening
   - Changes merged: optimistic-kv-lock; fallbacks now retry with exponential backoff and keep a local short-lived lock so repeated failures do not hammer underlying kernel.
   - Observed regressions: a small class of long-context reranker requests hit a retry loop; added exponential backoff cap and telemetry to spot runaway retries.

Operational Items / Action list (owners + eta):
- Evan: Turn on prefill_budget soft limit in canary config and monitor for the next 72h. ETA: 2029-11-15.
- Sofia: Implement size-aware eviction prototype and open A/B PR (linked_artifacts PR:1227). ETA: 2029-11-18.
- Marcus: Run a mixed-traffic jitter experiment with clock-slip randomization on two staging racks. Collect p50/p95/p99. ETA: 2029-11-16.
- Priya: Draft runbook amendment for KV cascade events and share with SREs for feedback. ETA: 2029-11-17.

Blockers / Help needed:
- We need product validation on increasing min-TTL for large items (impact on memory/cost). Tagging: @product-hosted-api for review.
- Observability gap: eviction waterfall doesn't show per-cohort origin; need small dashboard dev help. Requesting one front-end hours from observability.

Oncall notes (incident blips):
- 2029-11-09 02:14 UTC: transient p99 spike observed in canary pool; traced to a noisy customer test hitting prefill prewarm path. Auto-fallback engaged and recovered within 18s. Postmortem in JIRA-RT-2398.
- No customer-visible errors logged. SLA unaffected.

Quick wins for next week:
- Add a throttled prefill shadow mode that logs attempts but does not actually prefetch for 24h (to get a safe signal of prefill churn).
- Add a cohort tag to eviction telemetry so we can attribute cascades to traffic cohorts.

Meeting artifacts / references:
- Recording: slack call thread #serve-runtime-weekly, meeting 2029-11-07 (link in Confluence page).
- Perf artifacts: s3://redwood-inference/serve-runtime/benchmarks/2029-11-07-microbatch.csv
- Tests: PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/1227 (size-aware eviction)

Notes to self / rough thoughts:
- The choreographer approach is promising but we should be conservative in its default configs — prefilling is fundamentally speculative and the cost of wrong guesses amplifies when TTLs are short.
- Consider adding an adaptive-TTL that lengthens for items that are repeatedly re-requested over short windows; this may reduce the oscillation.
- Potential research spike: simulate cohort churn and prefill amplification with a synthetic cohort generator (Marcus + a small infra timebox).

Next sync preview (Wed 2029-11-14):
- Canary budget metrics from Evan; A/B results for size-aware eviction from Sofia; jitter experiment data from Marcus.

End of digest.

Appendix: short log snippets from daily standups this week:
- Tue: "Evan: dashboard is live; added an alert for eviction-rate > 5/s."
- Wed: "Sofia: kernel handshake tests green on perf bench but we saw one flaky reranker case."
- Fri: "Marcus: clock-slip randomization reduced p99 in the lab; rolling to staging next."
summary: Canary prefill choreographer reduces tail latency but exposed an eviction cascade under short TTLs; size-aware eviction and prefill-budget are next steps. Microbatch jitter mitigations show promise. Action owners assigned.
